description: Get an item and its comment tree as a threaded discussion, with child comments resolved recursively. Use depth 0 for an item-only lookup. A long thread comes back in pages: pass the returned nextCursor as cursor to continue.

cursor.description: nextCursor from a previous call, passed with the same itemId, to continue the traversal at the next unseen comment without repeating or skipping any. Omit to start from the top.

depth.description: How many levels of replies to resolve, at most 10 per call. 0 = just the item, no comments. 1 = direct replies only. A larger value is served at 10. Replies below the depth served are never fetched — to read them, raise depth up to 10, or call again with a comment from the deepest level returned, or one notice names, as itemId to drill into its subtree. Ignored when cursor is set: the depth the cursor was issued with applies.

itemId.description: ID of the story, comment, job, poll, or poll option to fetch the thread for.

maxComments.description: Maximum comments in one response, across all depth levels, at most 200 per call. A larger value is served at 200, and nextCursor continues from there. Highest-ranked top-level comments resolve first; replies fill in only after the level above is exhausted. A response also stops between comments to stay within a fixed 64,000-byte budget on each surface — all content[] text, nextCursor and the rest of the trailer included, and the structuredContent JSON — though its first comment is always returned whole. When either limit stops the traversal, nextCursor continues it.

name: hn_get_thread

cap.description: The maxComments value served: as passed, or 200 when maxComments was above that cap.

comments.description: Flat comment list ordered breadth-first by rank: highest-ranked top-level comments first, then their replies. Use depth/parentId to reconstruct nesting. With cursor, the page continues the same order.

items.description: A single comment in the thread with its tree position.

childCount.description: Number of direct child comments (may exceed what was resolved).

depth.description: Nesting level (0 = direct reply to root).

isOp.description: Present and `true` when the comment author submitted the story or poll the thread belongs to (OP replying within their own thread) — for a comment root, the story at item.storyId. Omitted otherwise, including when either author is missing. Most threads carry no OP replies, so absence usually means "not OP"; it means unknown when the thread's root has no author (a deleted story, for example) or when notice says replies are not marked.

parentId.description: Parent item ID: the root or another comment. It can name a dead or deleted comment, which this list omits while still returning its replies; pass that ID as itemId to see it marked.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `item_not_found`: HN reports no item exists for the given itemId. `invalid_cursor`: The cursor is not one this tool issued, was altered, or was issued for a different itemId than the one passed with it. `upstream_rejected`: The HN API answered with a 4xx status other than 429 — it rejected the request as built. `upstream_rate_limited`: The HN API answered with HTTP 429. `upstream_unavailable`: The HN API answered with a 5xx status. `upstream_html`: The HN API served an HTML error page with a 200 status, which it does under rate limiting or maintenance. `upstream_malformed`: The HN API answered with a 200 status and a body that is not JSON. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

failedIds.description: Comment and poll-option IDs whose fetch failed after retries or ran past the call's 50-second time budget, so neither they nor their replies are in this response. They are not deleted or missing and may load on a later call. Failed comments ride in nextCursor and are retried when you continue; without one, call again, or pass an ID as itemId to fetch that comment and its replies. Absent when everything the traversal reached loaded.

item.description: The root item: a story, comment, job, poll, or poll option.

dead.description: Present and `true` when the root is dead (flagged or killed); its replies are still walked. Omitted otherwise.

deleted.description: Present and `true` when HN reports the root deleted; its author and text are gone, but its replies are still walked. Omitted otherwise.

descendants.description: HN's count of live comments in the thread; dead and deleted comments are not counted.

options.description: For a poll root, its options with text and votes in parts order, resolved at every depth including 0. Deleted and dead options are kept and marked; an option whose fetch failed is listed in failedIds instead. Options do not count toward maxComments or totalLoaded.

dead.description: Present and `true` when the option is dead (flagged or killed). Omitted otherwise.

deleted.description: Present and `true` when the option was deleted. Omitted otherwise.

text.description: Option text (HTML stripped). Absent once deleted.

parent.description: For a comment root, the ID of the story or comment it replies to — pass it as itemId for the context above.

parts.description: For a poll root, its option IDs in HN order.

poll.description: For a poll-option root, the ID of its poll.

storyId.description: For a comment root, the ID of the story or poll its discussion belongs to — pass it as itemId for the whole thread, or as storyId to hn_search_content. Absent for other roots, and when the story could not be found (notice says why).

type.description: Item type: story | comment | job | poll | pollopt.

nextCursor.description: Pass as cursor, with the same itemId, to continue from the next unseen comment. Present when truncationReason is count, size, rate_limited, or time; absent on the last page.

notice.description: Traversal context: counts of deleted/dead comments dropped, the IDs that failed to load and how to retry them, then what stopped the traversal and how to continue — nextCursor for a count, size, rate-limit, or time-budget stop, or a larger depth or a comment id as itemId for a depth cut — noting when the maxComments or depth that stopped it was served at its per-call cap. Dead or deleted comments whose replies the depth limit cut are named by id, to pass as itemId, on the page that reaches them, since comments omits them. Absent when nothing was dropped, failed, or left unread.

totalAvailable.description: HN's count of live comments in the thread (descendants); dead and deleted comments are not counted. Absent for comment and job roots.

totalLoaded.description: Number of comments in this response (this page, when paging with cursor).

truncated.description: True when comments remain unread: reachable through nextCursor (truncationReason count, size, rate_limited, or time), or below the depth limit (depth). Absent on a terminal page — including a thread that loads in full at exactly maxComments.

truncationReason.description: Why the traversal stopped short: count = maxComments (or the 1,000-item ceiling per call) was reached; size = the page stopped between comments to keep content[] and structuredContent each within the 64,000-byte response budget; rate_limited = the HN API throttled the fetches; time = the call's 50-second time budget ran short because the HN API answered slowly or not at all; depth = replies lie below the depth limit, which nextCursor does not reach — raise depth or pass a comment id as itemId. When a cursor reason and a depth cut both apply, the cursor reason is reported.

title: Hn Get Thread
